content:
Former New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie (R) on Friday slammed Secretary of State Marco Rubio, accusing him of having blind loyalty to President Donald Trump and saying the Florida Republican “sold himself to get that job.”

He argued Rubio has not only “completely changed” his political points of view since the two lawmakers ran against Trump for the Republican presidential nomination in 2016 but also altered the manner that he expresses them in public. And he said Rubio has blatantly modified both just to “comport with the president.”

He continued, “Because from an issue of philosophical perspective, this is not the Marco Rubio I know, and it’s not the Marco Rubio who presented himself to the people of Florida and to the American people over the course of his whole career.”

Rubio unleashed on Trump ahead of the 2016 election, mocked his social media rants and called him a “con artist.” He has since routinely defended the Iran war and praised Trump, calling him “the greatest president in the history of the United States of America.”

Catch the bulk of this conversation starting at 34:04:

Christie appeared hesitant during the podcast to blame Rubio for his actions, particularly after host Dasha Burns brought up a notable moment from a 2016 presidential debate hosted by ABC News when he openly called out Rubio for his “memorized” statements.

“You see, everybody, I want the people at home to think about this — that’s what Washington, D.C., does,” the New Jersey Republican said at the time. “The drive-by shot at the beginning, with incorrect and incomplete information, and then the memorized 25-second speech.”

He continued at the time, “That is exactly what his advisers gave him.”

Christie was responding at the time to Rubio slamming then-President Barack Obama over his policies. He reacted Friday to the clip with some humility, as Burns asked if he thinks Rubio has “improved as a political athlete” since then — or if he’s still the “same old Marco.”

“Look ... at that time, Marco was 45,” Christie said Friday. “Now he’s 55. He’s a great dad and a great husband, and I think you learn a lot from all of those experiences. And so I’m sure Marco is better today than he was 10 years ago. I don’t have any doubt about that.”

He added, “I’m sure he’s better.”

Rubio recently defended Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth amid impeachment efforts. He has frequently justified Trump’s imperialistic stance toward NATO allies. And he was accused last week of spending more than $1 million in taxpayer dollars to watch his adult son play football.
